Nvidia lost about $190 billion in value in one day, after a spy story about its CEO.

US officials believe Jensen Huang had a relationship with Alice Huang, an executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore company that buys Nvidia chips, and US intelligence suspects she was working for China, The New York Times and the Financial Times reported. Over the weekend Huang told staff he had been unfaithful and apologized. Nvidia's board opened an investigation and said it has no reason to believe national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised. China calls the claims groundless, and no one has been charged. On Monday, November 9, Nvidia fell 4.27% to $178.67, about $190 billion off its value. But even before the weekend, the stock was about 25% below its October 6 peak, on worries about AI data center build-outs (Forbes). These are reported claims, not proven facts.

How much should a CEO's private life matter to a company's stock?
